summary: Compare Turán's localized and Lindelöf-conditional implications with the shell-count route, especially how the proof avoids cluster loss.
Read the remaining Section 36 remarks and determine what local zero-count bounds are known at a fixed positive strip offset.
Derive the correct unconditional local-count constant, its near-line behavior, and repair the full-zero-set conditional chain.
Require a reading or test deferred twice on one item to be performed or explicitly closed at the next development.
Choose a review's lead-section requirements from the pre-entry queue state when the review itself crosses the draining threshold.
Require a read source or distinguishing test for Goal progress judgments that a method is inapplicable or lacks a counterpart.
Specify and enforce how already-completed work is reported when a no-bearing rotation rule binds, preventing hidden continuation.
Make numerical controls state which theorem hypotheses vary and which remain fixed, exposing untested asymmetric cases.
Count an item's work across interleaved entries so switching items cannot evade the spell boundary.
Require Prevention when replies accept objections indirectly, not only when they contain explicit admissions.
Measure which newly changed tool lines the affected tests execute and report unreached lines before framework commits.
Profile claim checking and benchmark one C hot-path prototype against Python with byte-identical reports before considering a rewrite.
Audit control scripts run before their first commit and identify entries that incorrectly presented written-afterward expectations as predictions.
Read exact sources for zeta-zero symmetries, strip location, local counts and the absolutely convergent logarithmic-derivative identity.
Have the corrected count-listing entry reviewed against its final code and outputs, then correct any remaining false account.
Audit whether count-listing warnings prompted fresh checks; make ignored warnings refusals if the evidence warrants it.
Check the eight unaudited absence claims against the tree and transcript, including whether queue removals relied on them.
Compare review tests with their Obstacle and Attempt paragraphs so tests address the real gap and follow work already tried.
Compare complete written expectations, computed instances and displayed conditions with saved outcomes and universal claims.
Reject refines edges whose own notes deny either implication or describe incomparable statements.
Require framework measurements through the real command-line path, with saved output and counts of outcomes actually possible.
Flag whole-source conclusions based on partial or missing reads, including skipped ranges inside a proof.
Resolve shared queue identifiers by kind in guidance, closing, merging and picking; reject ambiguous bare IDs.
Calibrate new refusal checks on real recorded entries and report their historical refusal counts before committing them.
Show relevant older registered claims alongside later claims when orienting a queued item or next step.
Require review of post-review edits and flag hypothesis omissions beside cited statements rather than relying on an unread listing.
Detect continuation of a held item's attempt under a different queue ID after no-bearing rotation.
Match the specific search words claimed in Record search to actual session search logs, not merely the existence of some searches.
Check every part of a multipart proof before removing a hypothesis found unused in only one part.
Require the queue state to reflect the entry's follow-up before finalization, catching queue-update commands that never ran.
Track refused shell calls and require each to be rerun or explicitly disposed of before finalization or commit.
Require and record why exploratory scripts are run before committing their expectations, then surface those runs at finalization.
Require answer lines citing claims to quote the relevant registered statement, rather than naming only an ID and part.
Compare titles and prose citing a draft's numbered proposition parts directly with those parts' text.
Correct the reviewer-identified assessment overclaims, including unread imports, conditional counts, missing inductions and threshold gaps.
Search unregistered notebook passages as well as claim summaries before posing a review test already answered in passing.
Audit failure-status-only tests and require the intended refusal message so earlier prerequisite failures cannot masquerade as coverage.
Print every draft sentence beside its answer and cover titles and body passages interpreting the entry's own statements.
Recheck the seventeenth review's assessment corrections: constants, scale induction, source certainty, domains and cluster limitations.
Reject decisive tests with already-expected outcomes unless the review explicitly states that no test with an open outcome was found.
